inspiration.observed_pattern: An UPDATE JOIN reads from a nested derived source whose inner grouped query filters duplicate keys with HAVING and orders groups by their aggregate count.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Reauthored as a catalog-label repair. A nested derived source identifies duplicate tenant labels through a grouped HAVING query, then updates matching catalog rows with a deterministic record suffix. The source tables, identifiers, values, and operational meaning are newly authored.

fixture_notes: Tenant 11 has two duplicate labels and both matching catalog rows are repaired; tenant 12 has one duplicate group and is repaired; tenant 13 has no duplicate label and remains unchanged.
determinism_notes: All IDs and labels are fixed; the grouped source has a unique join key and the final state is ordered by catalog ID. No clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent schedules are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE catalog_rows (catalog_id INT PRIMARY KEY, tenant_id INT NOT NULL, label VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL, repaired_label VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL)
CREATE TABLE label_observations (observation_id INT PRIMARY KEY, tenant_id INT NOT NULL, label VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL)

steps.sql: UPDATE catalog_rows AS r JOIN (SELECT c.catalog_id, c.label FROM catalog_rows AS c JOIN (SELECT tenant_id, label, COUNT(*) AS duplicate_count FROM label_observations GROUP BY tenant_id, label HAVING duplicate_count > 1 ORDER BY duplicate_count DESC, tenant_id ASC) AS d ON c.tenant_id = d.tenant_id AND c.label = d.label) AS targets ON r.catalog_id = targets.catalog_id SET r.repaired_label = CONCAT(targets.label, '-', r.catalog_id)

checks.sql: SELECT catalog_id, tenant_id, label, repaired_label FROM catalog_rows ORDER BY catalog_id
SELECT tenant_id, label, COUNT(*) AS observation_count FROM label_observations GROUP BY tenant_id, label ORDER BY tenant_id, label
